source_text:
Γύμνασον ἐν λογισμοῖς τοὺς ὁπλίτας, οἳ ἐμπείρως ἔχουσι πρὸς τὴν μάχην· καὶ δεῖξον φοβερὸν
τὴν ἧτταν τῇ ἀπειλῇ τῆς αἰωνίου κολάσεως. Τὸν νικητὴν ἀνακήρυττε λαμπροῖς ἐπαίνοις, οἶδε γὰρ καὶ ἡ εὐφημία σπουδαιοτέρους ποιεῖν· καὶ τὸν ἐπηρεασθέντα θεράπευσον συμπαθῶς, οὐχ ἧττον γὰρ ἀπειλῆς ἐντρέπει συγγνώμη τὸν συνετόν. Μὴ κινήσῃ θυμῷ ἐφ' ἁμαρτήσαντι μαθητῇ, οὐ γὰρ ὅσιον ἑαυτὸν τιτρώσκειν πρὸ τῆς θεραπείας ἑτέρου· ἀλλὰ ἀνεξικάκως διόρθωσαι πρὸς τὸ ἀγαθόν· καὶ γὰρ ἰατρὸς θεραπεύει μὲν τὸ πάθος, οὐκ ἀγανακτεῖ δὲ πρὸς τὸν ἀκουσίως νοσήσαντα. Τέμνων ἰατρός, χωρὶς ὀργῆς τοῦτο ποιεῖ· καὶ ἐλέγχων διδάσκαλος μὴ μιγνύτω τῷ ἐλέγχῳ θυμόν.
thought_title: Train the soldiers and heal without anger
orientation: Evagrius is still addressing the leader, continuing the arming for combat before turning to the desert journey.
pass_a_gloss: Train the soldiers in thoughts, who are experienced with respect to battle; and show defeat as fearful by the warning of eternal punishment. Proclaim the victor with splendid praises, for praise also knows how to make more zealous; and heal with sympathy the one who has been injured, for forgiveness puts to shame the sensible man no less than warning. Do not be moved by anger at a disciple who has sinned, for it is not holy to wound oneself before the healing of another; but correct toward the good with patience under evil; for a physician heals the ailment, but feels no indignation toward the one who is sick involuntarily. A physician when cutting does this without anger; and a teacher when rebuking must not mix anger with the rebuke.

lemmas.gloss: the one who has been injured, harmed
with patience under evil, without retaliation

choices.why: keeps the mental training sense required by the arming context

choices.english: the one who has been injured
choices.why: passive participle means one harmed or ill treated in the struggle, not yet a loser
consistent rendering for the forbidden passion in both prohibition clauses
literal sense of bearing evil without retaliation when correcting

pass_b_english: Train your soldiers in their thoughts, so they meet the battle with skill, and make defeat look fearful to them by the warning of eternal punishment. Proclaim the victor with splendid praises, for praise too knows how to make men more eager, and tend the one who has been injured with compassion, for forgiveness shames a sensible man no less than a warning does. Do not turn in anger upon a disciple who has sinned, for it is no holy thing to wound yourself before healing another, but correct him toward the good with patience under evil. For a physician heals the passion and yet bears no anger toward the one who has fallen sick without willing it. When a physician cuts, he cuts without anger, and when a teacher rebukes, he must mix no anger into his rebuke.
